description: What single discount does the same?
solution_sketch: Successive discounts multiply the surviving fraction, they do not add: 0.70 x 0.80 = 0.56, so 56% of the price remains. A single discount of 100% - 56% = 44% has the same effect.
difficulty_rationale: The naive route adds the discounts and answers 50%, which is the trap; the careful naive route picks a price like 100, takes 30 off to get 70, then 20% of 70 = 14, giving 56 and 44% off - two subtractions and a percentage of a non-round number. The insight is that only the surviving fractions matter and they multiply: 7 x 8 = 56 remains, so 44 is lost. Reachable cold because 'take 30% off' immediately reads as 'keep 70%', and 0.7 x 0.8 is single-digit multiplication - but the wrong answer is attractive enough that nobody finishes in two seconds.
